giai_trinh.T04: Ảnh NASA 1943 (hầm gió Langley) là tư liệu gốc mà chủ dự án đã duyệt giữ ở G1 (ảnh NASA, không logo, có trong RIGHTS.md); phim tư liệu chủ ý đặt bằng chứng thật cạnh thế giới 3D cách điệu. Điểm cắt đã được làm mềm: đoạn 04 mở bằng chính chồng giấy 3D nối tiếp cuối đoạn 03, rồi hoà 1,4 s sang ảnh ngay chữ 'war'. Dải mẫu lấy cách nhau 1 s nên không thấy pha hoà. Người xem thứ ba không nêu điểm này.

R1.question: When a machine takes over a job and keeps its name, what happens to the people in that job, and can today's newest workers move on to new work the way the human computers and programmers did?

issues.note: Hard cut from the warm exterior of the lit windows to a close-up of a desk with a typewriter and a different, darker palette. The subtitle appears only after the cut, so the viewer does not yet know where this is.
The wide classroom shot cuts to a macro desk close-up while the narration is still mid-sentence ('to design the next test'). The shot change does not match the sentence.
The 3D desk scene switches abruptly to a sepia archival photo, a different visual language, with no transition.
The office of desks cuts to a dark archive corridor. The 'second kind of work' caption fades in late, and the corridor has no clear link to the narration about integration.
The archival IBM 704 photo cuts to a 3D hall of many desks. The 'arithmetic went to the machines' narration is illustrated by a full room of people calculating, which seems to show the opposite.
Cutting from the dark office to the programmer close-up while saying 'two job titles' is confusing. The two titles share one image, which separates them poorly.
Narration moves to 'the people just starting out' over an unchanged empty dark office. The picture does not show beginners.
The empty dark office is reused several times for abstract statistics, with nothing new to look at.

The empty dark office again carries long stretches of statistics narration (about 8:20 to 9:20), including R15.1 to R15.2 and R16.1 to R16.4. The same wide shot with little motion is used for too long.
The BLS quote cards are static text for a long stretch (R11.5 to R11.6, R12.1 to R12.3). Little new to look at.

R2.question: When a machine takes over a job and the job title stays the same, what happens to the people in it, and can the newest workers still move on with it?

issues.note: Hard cut from the stylised 3D desk to a sepia archival photo of the war-era wind tunnel. The change of look is abrupt and the photo has no establishing beat.

The caption '...to other workers, such as software developers' is spoken over a lingering shot of the same programmer desk, not over software developers. The picture does not show the subject being named.
R14.1-4 (about 16 s) hold the same dark ladder and lamp image while three statistics captions change over it. Nothing new appears in the picture.
The static quote card (R12.1-3, about 12 s, leading in from R11.5-6) is text only and has very little movement.
R17.5-7 show a near-identical dark night street with a lamp, with little change across about 12 s.

R3.question: When a machine takes over the work a job is named after, what happens to the job and to the people just starting out in it, as the word 'computer' and now 'programmer' kept the name while the work moved on?

issues.note: Hard cut from the lamplighter street back to a dark, modern night office with only the caption 'the third kind of work'. The lamplighter motif is dropped without a visual bridge, and the look changes from warm to cold blue.

The narration moves to AI taking over routine tasks, but the picture is the same empty-office wide shot used for the previous claims. Nothing on screen shows the new idea, and the jump in subject is hard to follow.
The dark ladder and lamp image holds for about 16 s (R15.1 to R15.4) while the -19% statistic and caption are read. There is almost no change in the picture.
The same dark office wide shot stays for about 16 s (R16.1 to R16.4) while three separate captions about young workers and routine tasks go by.
Several near-identical dark street frames in a row (R18.5 to R18.7) before the closing shot. They add no new information.
